title: incident-bot: integrate slo-toolkit on-call enrichment and runbook link heuristics
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: On-call messages lack actionable SLO/runbook context when incidents fire. This PR integrates the slo-toolkit enrichment APIs into incident-bot so that Pagerduty/Slack on-call summaries contain top-level SLO health, quick links to relevant runbooks, and heuristic scoring for likely runbook relevance. Goals: (1) surface SLO status and error budget burn in alerts, (2) provide the most-relevant runbook link directly in the alert, (3) minimize added latency to hot paths, and (4) be feature-flagged and configurable per-team. Changes include a new enrichment pipeline, caching layer with TTL and stale-while-revalidate, rate-limit protection when calling slo-toolkit, unit and integration tests, docs updates, and a migration step for enabling the feature per-service. Checklist: - [x] Add slo-toolkit client and enrichment layer - [x] Add caching + metrics (cache_hits, cache_misses, enrich_latency) - [x] Add feature flag and per-service config - [x] Add integration test against staging slo-toolkit - [x] Update incident-bot runbook and docs - [x] Add RBAC policy allowlist for slo-toolkit API calls Performance note: enrichment call is executed asynchronously for non-critical alerts and synchronously when alert severity is P0/P1. For synchronous path we added a 200ms circuit-breaker; best-effort enrichment is dropped on timeout to avoid blocking the alert flow. Related: ENG-8421 (on-call UX improvements), SUP-1198 (support case asking for runbook links).

Jonah Reed: Question - what guarantees do we provide about runbook freshness? If a runbook is updated upstream we could send stale links. Consider a short TTL and a stale-while-revalidate strategy.

Maya Chen (author): Implemented stale-while-revalidate and added runbook_hash metadata to the enrichment payload. Chose default TTL=5m with S-W-R window of 10m; documented in docs/runbooks/oncall-enrichment.md.
